newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia interbank rates rise as mkt remains tight.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia interbank rates rise as mkt remains tight.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates were sharply higher as the market remained tight after Bank Negara's intervention on Friday, dealers said on Monday.
They said one-week money was at 7.50/60 percent against 6.90/7.00 on Friday, two-week at 7.50 against 7.00/10 and one-month at 7.30 against 7.10.
Other rates rose more modestly, with three-month up at 7.30/35 percent against 7.20/25 and six-month at 7.35/40 against 7.25/28.
Dealers said a sharp rise in the overnight rate on Friday had triggered covering in slightly longer tenures.
The overnight rate on Friday ended at 8.5 percent.
Bank Negara intervened in the interbank market on Friday for a second time in one week to confirm that its support level for one-month rate had risen to 7.05 percent from 6.95.
"Merchant banks and finance companies are bidding the rates up, though there is still some lending by foreign banks," said a dealer with a local bank.
"One reason is because of the effect of Bank Negara pulling out money (on Friday)," he said.
Bank Negara returned to the market after nearly three months last Tuesday to borrow for a one-month deposit at 6.95 to 7.05 percent against 6.95 previously.
The central bank regularly intervenes in the local interbank market to keep a check on liquidity or set interest rates as part of its efforts to fight inflation.
But it had not been in the market since May 24, despite rising liquidity that has pressured rates downward, threatening to thwart the Bank's tight monetary policy.
